case_name: Dadu Dayal Mahasabha v Sukhdev Arya and Another
respondent:
Sukhdev Arya and Another
Supreme Court of India

17 November 1989
Civil Appeal No. 3901 of 1981
The Judgment was delivered by : L. M. Sharma, J.
This appeal by special leave is directed against the judgment of Rajasthan High Court dismissing a civil revision application filed by the appellant in the following circumstances.
The appellant, a registered Society, filed the suit out of which this appeal arises in the court of the District Judge, Jaipur City in respect of an immovable property through its the then Secretary which was numbered as Suit No. 11 of 1973. facts: The appellant, a registered Society, filed the suit out of which this appeal arises in the court of the District Judge, Jaipur City in respect of an immovable property through its then Secretary which was numbered as Suit No. 11 of 1973.
An election of the office bearers of the Society was held on 1.6.1973 and according to the appellant's case one Sri Laxman Das Swami was elected as the Secretary.
On 4.9.74 a prayer for withdrawing the suit was made by one Hari Narain Swami through another lawyer claiming to have been elected as the Secretary of the Society.

The trial court allowed the suit to be withdrawn and later, in the next election, another Secretary named Jeeva Nand Swami was elected, and when he learnt about the fate of the suit, an application was filed for recalling the order of withdrawal and restoring the suit to its file.
issues: Whether the trial court has jurisdiction to cancel the order permitting the withdrawal of the suit under its inherent power
Whether Hari Narain Swami was the duly elected Secretary of the appellant Society
petitioner_arguments: The application under s. 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, for restoration of the suit was maintainable and the error committed by the trial court while recording the finding on the merits of the case was such which the High Court ought to have rectified.

A dispute, relating to the election of the Secretary of the Society, had arisen between the parties which ultimately went before the Registrar of the Cooperative Societies, who decided the matter in favour of Laxman Das Swami and against Hari Narain Swami.
respondent_arguments: The trial court has no jurisdiction to recall its order permitting the withdrawal of the suit under its inherent power
Hari Narain Swami had been duly elected as the Secretary of the appellant Society and had, therefore, full authority to withdraw the suit
court_reasoning: A court has inherent power to correct its own proceedings when it is satisfied that in passing a particular order it was misled by one of the parties.
The principle has been followed in this country for more than a century.
holding: We, therefore, allow the appeal, set aside the impugned judgments of the trial court and the High Court and remit the matter to the trial court for reconsideration of the case on merits.
The parties shall be allowed to lead further evidence in support of their cases.
